text:
alex: Heads-up — I pushed a small perf-instrumentation spike proposal for token-level tracing. want quick feedback before i open a PR :wave:

maria: link?

alex: https://go/infra/ri-token-instr (draft) — TL;DR: capture a compact per-token envelope for ~0.5% sampled requests + full-sample for requests that hit error/latency SLOs. fields: kernel_id, batch_at_emit, kvcache_hit, ttft_ms, decode_ms, kernel_ms, prequeue_ms, postproc_ms, route_id, model_variant

dan: 0.5% seems reasonable for cost but how do we avoid sampling bias across routes / seq lengths?

alex: propose stratified sampling: keep 0.25% uniform + 0.25% skewed by route QPS and seq-length buckets (short/med/long). that reduces variance for rare long requests.

jess: do we need to include full prompt or any prompt-derived keys? PII concerns.

alex: no raw prompt. we'll hash prompt_id and include prompt_len_bucket only. store full payload only for SLO-triggered captures and mark for secure retention.

perf-bot: nightly-run: token-instr sampling enabled on staging at 0.5% (stratified) — 10k tokens captured so far :white_check_mark:

sam: quick question on attribution: how are we attributing kernel_ms vs decode_ms vs ttft_ms? those overlap in our current probes.

alex: good point. current plan: ttft_ms = time from request enter serving runtime -> first token emitted. decode_ms = per-token decode loop time (excluding kernel execution) measured on CPU side. kernel_ms = actual GPU kernel execution time as reported by the driver/kernel-trace when available OR estimated from our kernel instrumentation (start/stop on launch). prequeue_ms = time in queue before kernel launch. postproc_ms = time after kernel returns until token emit.

maria: can we tag kernel_id with exact kernel config (e.g., kernel_nobias_f16_q4a) rather than vague name? that would help correlate regressions to kernel builds.

alex: yes — kernel_id will be a stable string: <arch>:<kernel_family>:<quant>:<opt_flags> (examples in the doc).

dan: we should include batch_size_at_emit AND batch_size_at_kernel_start. due to continuous batching, they can differ and that changes kernel scheduling behavior.

alex: added both: batch_emit and batch_kernel_start.

jess: how about KV cache? if kvcache_hit is false for a token sequence, our latency profile changes a lot. can we include per-token kvcache_status: miss|hit|prefetch?

alex: yes, we'll use kvcache: hit/miss/prefetch and include kvcache_lookup_count (small int).

sam: overhead budget? emitting these envelopes adds CPU + network. what's acceptable?

alex: target <0.1% p99 tail on CPU time for sampled requests. envelope is tiny (~200 bytes). we batch metrics in-memory and stream to kafka with backpressure — feature gate per fleet.

perf-bot: quick sample results (staging, 10k tokens):
- p50(ttft_ms)=18ms, p95=78ms, p99=210ms
- kernel_ms median 6ms, but kernel_ms p99=135ms for kernel_family=B
- kvcache miss rate from sampled = 12% overall, 37% on long sequences >1024

maria: interesting — kernel_family=B shows up in p99. do we know kernel selection rule? is it falling back to a safe kernel for long sequences?

alex: yes, current runtime picks kernel_family=B for long sequences to avoid OOM. but B has less fused attention and higher tail variance.

dan: next step: dashboard tiles. i propose: token waterfall heatmap (x=time buckets, y=token index normalized) + overlay kernel_family color, plus faceting by route_id and kv_hit. Also per-route KPI tile: p50/p95/p99 ttft_ms and kernel_family distribution.

jess: add a correlated tile: kernel_build_hash -> p99 delta to quickly catch regressions after kernel rollouts. we can link to the build artifact and affected pods.

alex: agreed. also want an alert: if any route's p99(ttft) increases by >20% correlated with >10% change in kernel_family mix or kvcache miss rate.

sam: how will traces link to Jaeger/tempo? we need token-level spans but don't want to emit every token trace.

alex: token envelopes include trace_id. sampled envelopes will create a lightweight span in Jaeger using sampling decision. SLO-triggered captures will create full traces.

perf-bot: note: ensure we redact any hashed ids before sending to third-party monitoring. retention 30 days for sampled, 90 days for SLO captures.

maria: one more thought — batcher heuristics telemetry. we should include the batcher decision snapshot: queue_length_at_emit, heuristics_version. that helps reproduce why a token saw a particular batching outcome.

alex: added queue_len and batcher_version fields.

dan: can we get a minimal instrumentation snippet for runtime? put in the PR description to make adoption easier.

alex: sure, pseudo: 
```
emit_token_envelope({
  trace_id,
  route_id,
  model_variant,
  prompt_bucket,
  kernel_id,
  batch_kernel_start,
  batch_emit,
  kvcache,
  ttft_ms, decode_ms, kernel_ms, prequeue_ms, postproc_ms,
  queue_len, batcher_version
})
```

jess: looks good. let's also expose a sampled-stream API for engineers to pull raw sampled envelopes for ad-hoc analysis (RBAC).

alex: will add API + internal docs.

perf-bot: action items created: INFR-1423 (add envelope schema + producer), INFR-1424 (dashboard tiles: waterfall, kernel breakdown, per-route KPIs), INFR-1425 (sampling config + SLO-triggered capture policy).

maria: thanks — i'm going to run a focused sampling sweep on prod tomorrow morning for top 10 routes to validate the kvcache correlation. will post results here.

alex: awesome — please cc perf channel and paste short csv of route,kvcache_miss,p99 before/after.

dan: one last nit — make sure the metric names are consistent with metric catalog: use ri.infer.token.ttft_ms etc. add doc mapping soon.

alex: will do. thanks all :rocket:
